_comment: Mutations that put the AGPL-3.0 section 13 'the published source is the
running code' defect BACK into the branch, by breaking the ONE script
that makes the claim true.
THE DEFECT (measured 2026-11-07, review panel #5 on PR #64, and confirmed
by BOTH reviewers who answered): the container image is built from the
Docker build CONTEXT (the Dockerfile ends with `COPY . .`), while the
archive the offer publishes is the COMMITTED tree, and `git pull` never
removes untracked files. So a checkout with local changes produced a
running image containing files the published source did not contain -- and
the offer claimed they were the same code.
THE FIX is ops/scripts/record_deployed_commit.sh: it records the commit it
is about to build into .env, it REFUSES to stamp a checkout that is
not the committed tree, and it REFUSES to stamp a commit that was never
published. One implementation, shared by update.sh and the
MANUAL deploy sequence in AGENTS.md -- the manual path is the one the
operator actually uses, and a fix that only fires on the path nobody uses
is decorative (that was the SECOND half of the panel's finding).
THE SECOND DEFECT (measured 2026-11-09, review panel): the stamp took
`git rev-parse HEAD` with no check that the commit exists in the public
repository. The manual deploy path is `git pull origin main` with no
`git reset --hard`, so a local commit or a non-fast-forward merge leaves
HEAD unpushed -- and the offer points at
https://github.com/DiverseInc/DepthSight/archive/<commit>.tar.gz, which
is a 404 for a commit that was never pushed, while the page says the
commit is public. The script now asks `git branch -r --contains HEAD`
and refuses when no pushed ref contains the commit.
EVERY NEEDLE BELOW IS ASSERTED UNIQUE BEFORE USE: each occurs EXACTLY ONCE
in its file, measured against the file's bytes. A needle that matched two
sites would make the mutation meaningless, because the harness replaces
only the first hit; a needle that matched nothing would make the mutant
SKIP, and a SKIP is not a pass.
MUTANTS
A  the dirty-check refusal is removed, so a checkout with local changes
is stamped and the offer's claim becomes false. Killed by
test_an_untracked_file_is_refused and
test_a_modified_tracked_file_is_refused.
B  the missing-environment-file refusal is removed, so the script creates
a stub .env. That would start the application with NO configuration
at all -- a silent outage. Killed by
test_a_missing_environment_file_is_refused and
test_a_missing_environment_file_is_not_created.
C  the value is APPENDED instead of replaced, so .env ends up carrying
two DEPLOYED_COMMIT lines and the published commit is ambiguous.
Killed by test_an_existing_value_is_replaced_not_appended and
test_recording_twice_leaves_exactly_one_commit_line.
D  the carriage-return handling is dropped, so a Windows-edited .env has
its line endings rewritten. Killed by
test_a_crlf_environment_file_keeps_its_carriage_returns.
E  the project-root lookup is broken, so the script stamps the directory
it was started in instead of the project root. Killed by
test_run_from_a_subdirectory_it_still_stamps_the_root.
F  the refusal reports SUCCESS, so a dirty checkout is stamped anyway
and the deploy carries on. Killed by
test_an_untracked_file_is_refused.
G  the not-a-git-repository check is removed, so the script runs outside
a checkout and fails in a way that is not a clean refusal. Killed by
test_outside_a_git_repository_the_script_refuses.
H  the stamp is written to the wrong file, so the value never reaches the
.env the api service reads. Killed by
test_a_clean_checkout_records_the_commit.
I  the NOT-PUBLISHED refusal is removed, so a commit that was never
pushed is stamped and the offer publishes a 404 as the source.
Killed by test_a_commit_that_was_never_pushed_is_refused and
test_the_refusal_of_an_unpublished_commit_writes_nothing.
J  the published check asks about the PARENT commit instead of the
commit being deployed, so the commit that is actually stamped is
never the commit that was checked. Killed by
test_a_commit_that_was_never_pushed_is_refused (the pushed parent
passes the check, the unpushed child is stamped) and by
test_a_pushed_commit_is_stamped.
Run with:  python tools/mutation_harness.py tools/mutations/deployed_commit_script.json
NEVER run concurrently with a test run or tools/review_fanout.py -- both will
read a file that is mid-mutation and report on code that does not exist.

mutations.label: A: the dirty-check refusal is removed, so a checkout with local changes is stamped
B: the missing-environment-file refusal is removed, so the script creates a stub .env
C: the commit is appended instead of replaced, so .env carries two DEPLOYED_COMMIT lines
D: the carriage-return handling is dropped, so a Windows-edited .env loses its endings
E: the project-root lookup is broken, so the script stamps the directory it was started in
F: the refusal reports success, so a dirty checkout is stamped anyway
mutations.needle:
echo "  git checkout -- <path>   # discard ONE path's changes, deliberately" >&2
    exit 1
mutations.replace:
echo "  git checkout -- <path>   # discard ONE path's changes, deliberately" >&2
    exit 0

mutations.label: G: the not-a-git-repository check is removed, so the script runs outside a checkout
H: the stamp is written to the wrong file, so the value never reaches the api service
I: the not-published refusal is removed, so a commit that was never pushed is stamped
J: the published check asks about the parent commit, so the commit being stamped is never the one that was checked
